metas.name: 4 Straps
metas.note: The tent with 4 straps covers most of central-northern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Altai
metas.note:
In the town of Altai, you can see a range of dark, distant hills to the south and west and low rolling hills to the north and east. Additionally, it is common to see wet roads, as most of the coverage occurred after heavy rain.

NOTE: In older coverage, a unique tent can be seen, which is inflated on the left side.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Arid Steppe Rangeland
metas.note: You can find arid steppe rangeland, characterised by the coarse soil, patchy grass, and small shrubs, throughout southwestern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Arvaikheer
metas.note:
Arvaikheer is a large central town recognizable by the warm, green, and grassy landscape in gen 4, with low rolling hills in every direction. Often you can see the town’s ferris wheel in a park in the centre of town.

NOTE: In older coverage, a distinct camera smudge can be seen on the right side of the camera.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Backwards-Facing Snorkel
metas.note:
North of Ulaanbaatar you can find this car, which has the same blue tent as the eastern tent, but with a backwards-facing snorkel. The snorkel can sometimes be difficult to see, so use other additional clues such as rolling hills and forests to confirm the region.

NOTE: The highway in pink can have either the blue tent car or the tentless car with snow coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Baruun-Urt
metas.note:
Baruun-Urt can be identified by the towering building under construction in the centre of town (on the map its POI is called “Smile”) combined with the dry landscape.

NOTE: Similar buildings under construction can be found in other towns such as Chinggis but they are not as large and do not feature an orange tower crane like the Smile building.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Bayankhongor
metas.note:
The town of Bayankhongor, in central Mongolia, has an overall dry landscape and can be recognized from the nearby large dry hill to the east, with the Soyombo symbol inscribed onto it.

NOTE: In older coverage, a distinct camera smudge can be seen on the right side of the camera.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Car With Cage
metas.note:
A Street View car with a cage on top of the roof instead of a tent can be seen near Ulaanbaatar. West of Ulaanbaatar, the car will have a green camouflage sleeping bag on top of the cage (coverage highlighted in green). Additionally, all coverage with this car was taken during winter, with most of it being in snowy areas.

NOTE: The cage car can very rarely appear in Kharkhorin and Zuunmod.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Chinggis
metas.note:
Chinggis is a major town in the east with red straps on the front of the tent. It is a fairly dry and flat town with small hills to the north, and somewhat cloudy skies.

NOTE: Dundburd and Bayan-Ovoo are the only other towns with the same tent, but are much smaller towns with no paved roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Choibalsan
metas.note: Choibalsan is the only major city to have several concrete roads. In most parts of the city there is a visible smoke stack, which is in the southeast corner of the city. It appears to have just rained as the roads are slightly wet and the sky is overcast. Additionally, you may occasionally find unique pedestrian signs with a short figure over three stripes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Choir Highway
metas.note: The Choir Highway is the longest covered paved road in Mongolia, running from Nalaikh down to Zamiin-Uud on the Chinese border, and is mostly desert. The dry brown soil, lack of vegetation, clear skies, and general flatness are all characteristic of this road. Additionally, a railroad runs along the entire highway, which can be seen west of the highway north of Sainshand, and east of the highway south of Sainshand. Between the towns of Sainshand and Erdene there is some overcast coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Crop Fields
metas.note: Due to Mongolia’s harsh climate and terrain, crop fields are rare, but they do occasionally appear in the subdivisions of Selenge and Töv, near Ulaanbaatar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Dalanzadgad
metas.note: Dalanzadgad can be easily recognised by its distinct sunset coverage. Additionally it has a dry climate, fall-coloured grass, rocky hills to the south, some smoke stacks, and a unique loose tent cover on the left side.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Dariganga
metas.note: The town of Dariganga can be recognized by the distinctive hill present to the northwest of the town in an otherwise flat landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Darkhan
metas.note:
The city of Darkhan in northern Mongolia can be recognized by its distinct snow coverage. It is the third largest city in Mongolia and as such has many high-rising buildings and travelling cars.

NOTE: Other smaller towns can also have snow coverage but Darkhan is the only large city in Mongolia with snow coverage, apart from some Ulaanbaatar suburbs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Darkhan-Erdenet Hwy.
metas.note: The Darkhan-Erdenet highway can be identified by the low rolling hills, tall transmission towers, and occasional crop fields in the area. Additionally, most of the highway has winter coverage with the tentless car, light snow, and yellow grass. Beware that summer coverage can occasionally appear in the eastern half of the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Dense Forest
metas.note:
Khan Khokhii is a national park in northwestern Mongolia with some of the most dense forests in the country. It has partially cloudy skies, dark soil, and the western grey tent.

Keep in mind that the trails in this park do not appear on the map.

NOTE: There are other forests in Mongolia, but Khan Khokhii is one of the biggest and one of the only areas where you can be completely surrounded by trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Dry, Rugged Hills and Mountains
metas.note: These dry, rugged hills and mountains are common to see in far western Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Eastern Grassland Car
metas.note: In the eastern grasslands, the Street View car has a light blue tent and a forward-facing snorkel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Empty Roof Racks
metas.note: The roof racks of the Street View car are very useful as they can effectively split Mongolia in half. The presence of rubber inlays in the roof racks are generally found in the west, while empty roof racks are generally found in the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Erdenet
metas.note:
Erdenet is the second largest city in Mongolia. As such, it has many multistory buildings that can be seen from across town, a large stadium, and a ferris wheel in the south of the city. It is surrounded by large barren hills to the south and to the north, and was covered on a cloudy day in the winter, meaning all vegetation is dead.

NOTE: Erdenet can look very similar to Darkhan and Ulaanbaatar, but the lack of snow distinguishes it from Darkhan, while the cloudy skies and lack of rubber inlays on the roof racks can be used to distinguish it from Ulaanbaatar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Extremly Snowy Coverage
metas.note: The Mandalgovi Highway runs south of the capital and was covered during a blizzard, making it extremely snowy and foggy. It also has a deep blue tent, which is found along this entire road, and a flat landscape which can differentiate it from other snowy roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Fall Coverage
metas.note:
Fall coverage in Mongolia gives rise to very distinct orange-coloured trees and grass, and can only be found in a few areas; mostly between the towns of Lun and Hatgal, with some fall coverage around Ulaanbaatar. Trees are more commonly seen the further north you are.

NOTE: Some of the generation 4 coverage in Ulaanbaatar was also taken in the fall.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Forests
metas.note: You can find forests, typically surrounded by grassy fields, all around northern Mongolia. Generally these will be Siberian Larches, with pines and birches being common as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park
metas.note: The Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park, in the far south of Mongolia, features bright orange sand and sand dunes. There are two separate spots covered in the park: one in the middle just north of Sevrei, which has distant southern mountains, and the other in the far southwest corner of the park, which has a Jeep follow car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Grey Tent Car
metas.note: A Street View car with a grey tent and hooks on the tent can only be found in western Mongolia. It is the most common car to have the netted spare tire.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Hatgal
metas.note: Hatgal is a small lake town on the Khuvsgul Lake. It can be recognized from its fall coverage with orange trees and grass, and the large lake in the northeast, where the Khuvsgul Ice Festival is held every year.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Hook Straps Car
metas.note: If the grey tent has hook straps angled downwards, you should be in southwestern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Khalkhgol
metas.note: The town of Khalkhgol in far east Mongolia can be recognized by its flat, green landscape with low rolling hills and a giant sword statue visible in the distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Khovd
metas.note:
Khovd is a large, dry and shrubby town, in western Mongolia, that can be identified by the very distinct rocky, red-tinted hills, present to the north of town.

NOTE: The nearby Khar-Us, Tugrug, and the samely named Khovd have similar landscapes but are much smaller towns.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Knot on Both Straps
metas.note: The tent with a knot on both straps covers most of southwestern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Lakes/Rivers
metas.note: Lakes and rivers are much more common in western Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mandalgovi
metas.note: Mandalgovi is a large desert town with notably cloudy coverage. It’s the only large desert town apart from Dalanzadgad which is not on the Choir Highway, and it has a deep blue tent instead of the tentless car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mandalgovi Rd.
metas.note: The other main desert highway in Mongolia runs through Mandalgovi, and can be differentiated from the Choir Highway by its cloudy skies, darker pavement, and deep blue tent instead of the tentless car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Murun
metas.note:
Murun is a town in the north built on a north-south grid with a large jagged hill nearby to the north. It has a lot of alley coverage with dark cloudy skies and muddy, unpaved roads.

NOTE: Murun occasionally has sunny coverage where it isn’t cloudy, so consider other clues as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Narrow Dirt Trails
metas.note:
Around the town of Bugant is a large forest that stands out for having narrow dirt trails with close trees, typically on both sides, in a way that can appear quite Russian. Additionally, it is very common to see birches around this area.

Keep in mind that the dirt trails in this forest do not appear on the map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Netted Spare Tire
metas.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A netted spare tire shown in red
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Night Coverage
metas.note:
Mongolia has four main areas of nighttime coverage. Those areas are:

  • Northwest of Murun
  • West of Dashbalbar
  • South of Baruun-Urt
  • East of Dariganga

All of these locations are driving towards town. Driving direction and car meta can help identify which area of nighttime coverage you are in.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: No Hooks Car
metas.note: If the grey tent has no hooks on the left side and is billowing from the wind, you will be on the road between Khovd and Ölgii or around the town of Tugrug.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: No Spare Tire
metas.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

Without a spare tire shown in blue
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: No Tent Car
metas.note:
A Street View car with no tent can be seen in and around the capital city. It is generally found on a northwest diagonal going through Ulaanbaatar. Southeast of Ulaanbaatar, on the Choir highway, the car will have a double mirror on the left as well as a backward facing snorkel.

Driving direction is especially useful with this car as it is always travelling away from the capital.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Off-Road Desert Coverage
metas.note: There are several areas with off-road desert coverage in southern Mongolia. Most of this coverage is directly south or east of the town of Mandalgovi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Ölgii
metas.note: Ölgii is a large town in the west, that is surrounded by close, dry rocky mountains. Towards the south end of town, there is a tall red & white radio tower, that can be seen from all across town and is quite distinct to Ölgii.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Open Zipper
metas.note: You can find a tent with an open zipper in central Mongolia, near the town of Khorgo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Orange Short Grass
metas.note:
The Millenium Road runs just west of the town of Lun, and has late fall coverage, combined with a dry climate that gives it characteristic orange short grass. The silver tent, clear skies, and general flatness with low rolling hills also help in identifying this road. The sun gradually sets as the car continues west until it becomes sunset at the end of the road.

NOTE: At the end of the road, the car continues travelling northwest up to Murun on off-road dirt trails.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Paved Desert Road
metas.note: There are a couple of paved desert roads in southern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Red Tensioner Strap
metas.note:
The tent will have red tensioner straps at the front around the city of Chinggis.

NOTE: The Chinggis-Baganuur highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: River Valley
metas.note: This beautiful river valley, just west of Lake Hatgal in the Khoridol Saridag mountains, is very recognizable from the surrounding rocky cliffs and forests, and the ground that is completely covered in pebbles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Roof Decal Car
metas.note: Generation 4 coverage in the capital uses a silver truck with an ornate blue & white roof decal, with a snorkel and long antenna on the front right. While the unique roof can be seen in most locations, some locations blur most of the car, leaving only the snorkel and antenna visible. This car can only be found around Ulaanbaatar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Roof Racks With Rubber
metas.note: The roof racks of the Street View car are very useful as they can effectively split Mongolia in half. The presence of rubber inlays in the roof racks are generally found in the west, while empty roof racks are generally found in the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Sainshand
metas.note: Sainshand is the largest town in the desert region and it has a dry climate, many buildings, and paved roads. A dry ridge separates the northern and southern parts of the town, distinguishing Sainshand from other desert towns that are mostly flat. In the downtown area you can find a miniature pink eiffel tower.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Silver Car
metas.note: Generation 4 coverage in western Mongolia uses a silver pick-up truck with a big light blue tent. Different variations of the tent can be useful for narrowing down the region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Silver Tent Car
metas.note:
A Street View car with a bright silver tent is generally found in central and northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: The Bulgan Highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Single Knot Car
metas.note:
The tent with 2 straps and a single knot in the straps covers most of northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: Occasionally, camera stitching can hide the knot.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Single Strap Spare Tire
metas.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A single strap spare tire shown in green
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Small Shrubs
metas.note:
East of Uvs lake, you can find a lot of these small shrubs and patchy grass in a somewhat flat landscape.

NOTE: Similar shrubs can be found around Shaazgai Lake, but that area is considerably more hilly.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Snow Coverage
metas.note: Snow coverage is mostly found around Ulaanbaatar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Snow-Capped Peaks
metas.note: In the westmost part of Mongolia, there is some very remote coverage showcasing the tallest mountains in Mongolia where you can see glaciers and snow-capped peaks. This area also has a unique Street View car with a green or black bag above the right side roof racks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Spare Tire With No Strap
metas.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A spare tire with no strap shown in orange
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Strap In Clump
metas.note: The tent with the lower strap in a clump covers most of central-southern Mongolia, along the road from Ulaanbaatar to Altai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Straps-Layout
metas.note:
The eastern region can be further divided into several smaller areas based on the layout of the orange roof rack straps. These straps can be seen by looking straight down.

NOTE: Orange straps can be found in the west as well, this tip is only useful for the eastern car with a blue tent from the previous tip.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Sükhbaatar/Altanbulag
metas.note:
Sükhbaatar and Altanbulag are two neighbouring towns in the north near the Russian border. They have dry, forested hills all around and heavy overcast coverage. Sukhbaatar is completely overcast while Altanbulag is slightly less cloudy.

NOTE: Murun and Choibalsan are two other towns that also have overcast coverage, but lack forested hills and have different Street View cars.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Tosontsengel
metas.note: The small, hilly town of Tosontsengel, frequently has red-tinted roads and uses these unique lamp posts that have a wavy design.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Tsetserleg
metas.note: In the central town of Tsetserleg, you will see these distinct rocky, rugged hills, with small trees growing on them to the north. It has very clear skies and the neighbourhoods can often be seen on the hilly slopes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Ulaanbaatar
metas.note: The capital city, Ulaanbaatar, is by far the biggest city in Mongolia, with about 50% of the entire country's population living in it. As such, its urban development and sheer size is unlike anywhere else in Mongolia. The cityscape is bustling with many high rise buildings, chain stores, travelling cars, buses, and pedestrians, as well as clean roads and sidewalks. Meanwhile, the suburbs can be recognized from the vast yurt districts in hilly areas. Generation 4 coverage is common, however Generation 3 winter coverage is also common to see in the suburbs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Ulaangom
metas.note:
Ulaangom is a northwestern town with large, distant, dark mountains to the southwest. Additionally, these distinct double lamp posts with a blue or green painted base can frequently be seen in Ulaangom.

NOTE: Rarely, double lamp posts can be found in other cities such as Baruun-Urt and Chinggis, but these towns have flat landscapes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Uliastai
metas.note: Uliastai is a central-western Mongolian town, surrounded by large, green nearby hills. It is common to see a decent amount of trees or the river that runs through the town. In the centre of town, you can find a small hill with the Soyombo symbol inscribed on it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Vast Grassy Fields
metas.note: Small dirt tracks within flat, vast grassy fields are mainly found in far eastern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Yolyn Am Valley
metas.note: Yolyn Am Valley is located just west of Dalanzadgad and can be identified by the extremely foggy coverage, and having dark coloured soil and hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Zamiin-Uud
metas.note:
The desert town of Zamiin-Uud on the border with China has unique sailboat lamp posts featuring a golden flower pot around them. Often, white signs with Mongolian folded script can be seen attached to these lamp posts.

NOTE: The other desert towns of Choir and Sainshand look similar to Zamiin-Uud and have the same Street View car but use different lamp posts. Choir can be identified by its blue lamp posts and Sainshand by its white lamp posts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.
